Alex / team —

Quick comments after a first-pass look at terraform-plan-redwood-net-v2.txt and the module checklist:

- State & secrets: confirm remote state backend (S3 with SSE-KMS) + state locking (Dynamo/consul). If Brightwell prefers self-hosted Consul, we need ACL details.
- IPAM: YAML mapping in the module has hardcoded /24s for tenant VLANs — ask Brightwell to supply an IPAM extract or we should parameterize via a map variable (tenant_ips).
- MTU & overlay: Calico + BGP peering is fine but note VM-to-pod MTU mismatch on jumbo frames. Add MTU config and test plans to the runbook.
- Naming: module outputs use short names; prefer full prefixing (redwood-<env>-<component>) to avoid cross-account collisions.
- BGP: ensure community tags and route filters are explicit in Terraform so we don't accidentally accept imported routes from other tenants.

I'll attach a short snippet of local policies we enforce in our modules and a sample terraform plan with sensitive diff lines redacted (see attachment stub). For the pilot, recommend we run the plan in a read-only sandbox with state pulled from a non-prod bucket.

Laura

Team —

Couple of Helm/angle-of-deployment notes after scanning helm-values-controlplane-sample.yaml:

- Replicas & probes: make liveness/readiness probes configurable (they're currently hardcoded). For the pilot we want conservative probe timeouts to avoid churning during base-network changes.
- Canary: we'll run control-plane chart canary using 10% traffic and a 15-minute observation window before promoting. We'll need an ingress rule template from Brightwell for SNI-based routing so canary traffic is isolated to a subset of hosts.
- Secrets: don't render secrets in Helm templates — use Vault CSI + Kubernetes secrets sealed by your KMS. Document the secret bootstrap flow in the runbook (we'll draft examples).
- Compatibility: the chart assumes CNI supports hostNetwork for a sidecar; verify your Calico config allows hostNetwork for the metrics exporter.

On CI gating — I propose a two-phase job set:
1) infra-validate (terraform fmt/validate + helm lint + static ansible-lint) — required.
2) infra-smoke (deploy to ephemeral namespace + run infra-smoketest harness) — gate only if infra-validate passes.

I'll add a sample Jenkinsfile snippet to run infra-smoke and share before the call.

— Soojin

All —

Putting forward a concrete CI/CD gating + rollback recipe we can validate on Wednesday's call. Steps below assume Terraform modules live in a mono-repo and Helm charts in a chart repo; Ansible roles are invoked from the control-plane job.

Pre-merge pipeline (GitHub Actions):
- PR must pass terraform fmt/validate, terraform init -backend=false, helm lint, ansible-lint.
- Run a static policy check (sentinel/OPA) to ensure no open security groups and required tags exist.

Post-merge pipeline (Jenkins orchestrator):
1) terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan (remote-state read only), upload plan artifact.
2) infra-smoke job: create ephemeral namespace (k8s) + apply helm chart with test values, run smoke tests (connectivity, basic API auth, healthchecks).
3) approval gate (manual) if plan includes network or BGP changes — require two approvers (Brightwell SRE + Redwood infra lead).
4) terraform apply (with flags to enforce -auto-approve only from Jenkins service account).
5) Ansible role run for node init (idempotent, check mode first).

Rollback quick commands (to include in runbook):
- terraform destroy -target=module.redwood_control_plane --state=pilot-state (only after coordination)
- helm rollback <release> <revision>
- ansible-playbook rollback-playbook.yml -e "target_group=pilot"

Secrets & bootstrap: use Vault with AppRole for Jenkins; store Vault root accessor in HSM/KMS and restrict token lifetime. We'll include sample AppRole policy in runbook_v1.md.

I'll attach a sketch of the Jenkinsfile and the exact CLI snippets in the runbook.

— Dev
